title: Boss: the network on-call
summary: Diagnose a production request end to end: URL, firewall, balancer and curl output.

steps.title: On call
body: Tonight's pager has three problems. Each step builds on helpers from this track; paste what you need.

steps.title: Where does this request go?
prompt: Write `string Route(string url, Dictionary<string, string> dns, List<(string Prefix, string Pool)> routes)` for a layer 7 balancer:
1. Parse the host and path from `url` (scheme `http`/`https`, optional port, optional query).
2. Look the host up in `dns` (host -> IP). Its keys are lowercase, so lowercase the host first. No entry: return `"NXDOMAIN"`.
3. Otherwise return the pool of the **longest** route prefix the path starts with, or `"default"`.
The result for a hit is `"{ip} {pool}"`, e.g. `"203.0.113.10 api"`.
starter: string Route(string url, Dictionary<string, string> dns, List<(string Prefix, string Pool)> routes)
solution: string Route(string url, Dictionary<string, string> dns, List<(string Prefix, string Pool)> routes)
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoDns = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["shop.example"] = "203.0.113.10" };
var dojoRoutes = new List<(string Prefix, string Pool)> { ("/api", "api"), ("/api/admin", "admin"), ("/static", "cdn") };
Dojo.Eq("api", "203.0.113.10 api", Route("https://shop.example/api/orders?x=1", dojoDns, dojoRoutes));
Dojo.Eq("longest prefix", "203.0.113.10 admin", Route("https://SHOP.example:8443/api/admin/users", dojoDns, dojoRoutes));
Dojo.Eq("default", "203.0.113.10 default", Route("http://shop.example", dojoDns, dojoRoutes));
Dojo.Eq("unknown host", "NXDOMAIN", Route("https://nope.example/api", dojoDns, dojoRoutes));
hints: Reuse your URL parsing from the HTTP module.
`OrderByDescending(r => r.Prefix.Length)` picks the most specific route.

steps.title: Read curl -v
prompt: Write `string Diagnose(string curlOutput)` that reads the lines of a `curl -v` transcript and returns the **first** problem:
- a line containing `Could not resolve host` -> `"dns"`
- a line containing `timed out` -> `"firewall or routing"`
- the response status line (starts with `< HTTP/`) with a status >= 500 -> `"server error {code}"`, 400-499 -> `"client error {code}"`
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("dns", "dns", Diagnose("* Could not resolve host: shpo.example\ncurl: (6) Could not resolve host"));
Dojo.Eq("refused", "nothing listening", Diagnose("*   Trying 10.0.0.5:8080...\n* connect to 10.0.0.5 port 8080 failed: Connection refused"));
Dojo.Eq("timeout", "firewall or routing", Diagnose("*   Trying 10.0.0.5:22...\n* Connection timed out after 30000 milliseconds"));
Dojo.Eq("tls", "tls", Diagnose("* Connected\ncurl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate"));

Dojo.Eq("502", "server error 502", Diagnose("* Connected
> GET / HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< server: nginx"));
Dojo.Eq("404 over h2", "client error 404", Diagnose("> GET /x HTTP/2\n< HTTP/2 404\n< content-length: 0"));
Dojo.Eq("ok", "ok", Diagnose("> GET / HTTP/2\n< HTTP/2 200\n< x-cache: HIT"));
hints: Check each line in order and return at the first match.
On `< HTTP/...` the status is the second space-separated word after `<`, i.e. index 2.

steps.title: Can this packet get in?
prompt: Put it together. Write `string Trace(string sourceIp, int port, List<string> firewallRules, Dictionary<int, string> listeners)`:
- evaluate the firewall (rules as in *NAT, firewalls, CDNs and curl -v*: `action proto port cidr`, protocol is always `tcp` here; no match = deny). If denied, return `"timeout"` (dropped silently).
- if allowed but no listener on `port`, return `"refused"`.
Include `ToUInt`, `InCidr` and your `Evaluate` from that lesson.
starter: // paste ToUInt, InCidr and Evaluate here
string Trace(string sourceIp, int port, List<string> firewallRules, Dictionary<int, string> listeners)
solution: if (!int.TryParse(p, out int n) || n < 0 || n > 255) throw new FormatException("bad octet " + p);
string Evaluate(List<string> rules, string proto, int port, string sourceIp)
if (protoOk && portOk && InCidr(sourceIp, p[3])) return p[0];
string Trace(string sourceIp, int port, List<string> firewallRules, Dictionary<int, string> listeners)
return listeners.TryGetValue(port, out var name) ? $"connected to {name}" : "refused";
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoFw = new List<string> { "allow tcp 443 0.0.0.0/0", "allow tcp 22 10.0.0.0/8", "allow tcp 8080 10.0.0.0/8" };
var dojoLs = new Dictionary<int, string> { [443] = "nginx", [22] = "sshd" };
Dojo.Eq("public https", "connected to nginx", Trace("8.8.8.8", 443, dojoFw, dojoLs));
Dojo.Eq("internal ssh", "connected to sshd", Trace("10.1.2.3", 22, dojoFw, dojoLs));
Dojo.Eq("external ssh", "timeout", Trace("8.8.8.8", 22, dojoFw, dojoLs));
Dojo.Eq("allowed, nothing listening", "refused", Trace("10.1.2.3", 8080, dojoFw, dojoLs));
Dojo.Eq("not in rules", "timeout", Trace("10.1.2.3", 5432, dojoFw, dojoLs));
hints: Firewall first: a deny means the client hears nothing.
Then look the port up in `listeners`.
